title: Crumb coat and smooth buttercream sides
subtitle: The two-stage approach to a clean, crumb-free finish on a layered cake
excerpt: A crumb coat is a thin layer of buttercream applied to seal the cake crumbs before the final coat. After 30 minutes in the fridge, the crumbs are locked under a firm shell and the final coat goes on cleanly. Smooth sides come from a bench scraper held against the turntable while the cake spins.
sourceNotes: The crumb coat technique is a standard method in professional and home cake decoration, widely taught as the first step in producing a clean-finished layered cake.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: A crumb-coated cake can be refrigerated overnight before the final coat is applied.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thin first layer of buttercream applied over the whole cake to seal in loose crumbs. Once chilled and firm, it acts as a clean base for the final decorative coat.

content.text: is the first coat of buttercream on a stacked layered cake. It does not need to be neat. Its job is to trap the loose crumbs from the cake's surface so they do not appear in the final finish. The final coat goes on smoothly over the crumb coat once it has chilled.

Level each cake layer with a serrated knife if they have domed. Place the first layer on a cake board on the turntable. Spread a generous layer of buttercream on top, smooth it level with the icing spatula, and add the next layer. Repeat for all layers. Press the stack lightly to make sure it is level before proceeding.

Apply a thin layer of buttercream over the entire cake with the icing spatula, working it into any gaps between layers. The coat should be no more than 2 to 3 mm thick. Do not worry if crumbs appear in the buttercream, that is expected. The point is to cover every exposed crumb surface. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
The final coat and smooth sides
Apply a thick final coat of buttercream all over the chilled cake with the icing spatula. Build the sides up slightly thicker than the finished thickness you want.

Hold the bench scraper vertically against the side of the cake, with the bottom edge touching the turntable. Spin the turntable in one direction while holding the scraper still. The excess buttercream collects on the scraper.
Wipe the scraper clean after each pass. Repeat, adding more buttercream to any low spots with the spatula. Keep going until the sides are smooth and straight.
Smooth the top with the icing spatula, pulling inward from the edges to flatten any raised ridge left by the scraper.
